rounds.hypothesis: Per diagnose: `IpcNamespace::validate_sem_set` is a stub returning Ok unconditionally, so no SysV IPC permission check exists. Implementing Linux's `ipcperms()` as a predicate on the shared `IpcPermission` type, folding the caller's semflg into a requested triplet and reordering the semget checks to match `ipcget_public`, should make subtest 1 return EACCES.
rounds.change: Added `IpcPermission::check_access` (kernel/src/ipc/mod.rs) selecting one mode triplet by euid then group, with a `CAP_IPC_OWNER` override via the existing `lsm_hooks::on_capable`; de-stubbed `validate_sem_set` to call it; at the semget site replaced the hardcoded `ALTER|READ` with the fold `((mode>>6)|(mode>>3)|mode)&0o7` and moved the check below the IPC_EXCL and num_sems tests; threaded credentials/`PosixThread` through `with_sem_set` to its 6 semctl and 2 sem.rs call sites; gave semop `ALTER`/`READ` from its existing `is_alter`. Note: the worktree already contained a partial, non-compiling draft of `check_access` (it referenced a nonexistent `self.cgid` field) despite diagnose.json reporting a clean worktree; that draft was completed and corrected rather than discarded.
rounds.outcome: still failed: semget02 5 passed / 1 failed, unchanged. Asterinas correctly clears capabilities on setuid, so the child lacked CAP_IPC_OWNER and the check did fire - but `on_capable` returns EPERM and `check_access` propagated it, whereas the test (and Linux's `ipc_check_perms`) expects EACCES.

rounds.hypothesis: The predicate and its placement are right; only the errno is wrong. Linux's `ipcperms()` reports a permission failure as EACCES regardless of why the capability override was unavailable, so the capability hook's EPERM must not be propagated - it must be consumed as a boolean.
rounds.change: In `check_access`, treat `on_capable` as a predicate (`.is_ok()`) and return EACCES explicitly when the mode bits do not grant the access and the capability is absent. Also gave `PermissionMode` an `EXEC = 0o001` bit so `from_bits_truncate` cannot silently drop the low bit of a folded triplet, and factored the group test into `is_in_group_of` so the supplementary-group lock is taken once.
rounds.outcome: green: semget02 6 passed / 0 failed, matching the host's 6/6, and `All conformance tests passed.`

layer: The shared System V IPC permission layer, as `owning_layer` specified: the predicate lives on `IpcPermission` in kernel/src/ipc/mod.rs and is invoked from `IpcNamespace::validate_sem_set`. `IpcPermission` is the one type that stores key/uid/gid/cuid/cguid/mode for all three IPC object kinds, so the future msgget and shmget lookup paths inherit the rule instead of re-deriving it - the same placement Linux uses by putting `ipcperms()` in ipc/util.c rather than in sem.c.
generalizes: The predicate reads only the object's stored credentials and the caller's, so it holds for every caller rather than for semget's path. It is what fixes the six `semctl` operations that were already passing meaningful modes into the stub (IPC_STAT, SEM_GETPID, SEM_GETVAL, SEM_GETNCNT, SEM_GETZCNT with READ; SEM_SETVAL with ALTER) - before this, any process could read or overwrite any semaphore set in its namespace. `semop` needed its own edit because it passed `empty()`; it now derives ALTER or READ from the `is_alter` it already computed, matching Linux's `alter ? S_IWUGO : S_IRUGO`. Measured beyond the target: gvisor `semaphore_test` is green in its CI configuration (21 passed; the only 8 failures under an unfiltered run are exactly the 8 already-blocklisted cases, verified line by line against blocklists/semaphore_test), the full `AUTO_TEST=regression` suite passes including test/initramfs/src/regression/ipc/sem and security/namespace/ipc_ns_sem, and the three other enabled LTP semaphore tests (semget01, semctl07, semop03) pass alongside semget02 at 33/33 subtests. A stash-and-rebuild A/B against the base commit on the still-blocked tests showed semctl02 moving fail -> pass and semget05/semop01/semop02/semctl01 unchanged, so the change fixes one additional blocked test and regresses none. Deliberately left alone, matching Linux: creation carries no check (`create_sem_set` and the `insert_at` arm, per `ipcget_new`), and `semctl(IPC_RMID)` keeps its own euid==uid||euid==cuid rule, which Linux enforces separately in `ipcctl_obtain_check` with a CAP_SYS_ADMIN escape - a related gap this fix does not silently absorb.
fix_summary: Implements Linux's `ipcperms()` as `IpcPermission::check_access`, designed against Asterinas's own abstractions rather than transplanting Linux's structure: the requested access is expressed as the existing `PermissionMode` bitflags (already in Linux's folded low-three-bit form) instead of a raw mode word, and the CAP_IPC_OWNER override goes through the established `lsm_hooks::on_capable` / `CapableContext` hook against the namespace's owning `UserNamespace`, the same way `IpcNamespace::new_clone` checks CAP_SYS_ADMIN - so the check is namespace-scoped by construction. Exactly one mode triplet applies, chosen by euid against uid/cuid, else by the group test, else the 'other' triplet left unshifted; `is_in_group_of` mirrors `in_group_p` by testing fsgid before the supplementary set, which is the one place the two halves of Linux's predicate read different credential fields. A capability failure is consumed as a boolean and reported as EACCES, because the hook's native EPERM is not the errno IPC lookup reports. Two secondary corrections at the semget call site: the requested access is now the caller's semflg folded into a triplet rather than a hardcoded ALTER|READ, and the permission check moved below the IPC_EXCL and num_sems tests so error precedence matches `ipcget_public` - without which an unprivileged IPC_CREAT|IPC_EXCL against an existing mode-0 set would return EACCES where Linux returns EEXIST. `PermissionMode` gained an `EXEC = 0o001` bit so a folded triplet cannot lose its low bit to `from_bits_truncate`.
